panels.title: Resources: each Cloud Run service's CPU, memory, instances, concurrency and start-up (open a row)
No disk on a Cloud Run service

options.content: **Cloud Run services have no disk.** A file a container writes is held in its memory, so a service's "disk space" is its **Memory** chart: files that grow show as memory climbing to the red line, then as a container killed for memory. Real disk is on the databases (each one's disk space is on its area's page and on Databases) and in the buckets. A **red line** is the line the pager uses (tpa-platform's alert policies); a **grey line** is a limit the service is set to.

panels.title: Resources · auth: CPU, memory, instances, concurrency, start-up
CPU (p99, p95, p50)
panels.description: auth's container CPU, the share of its CPU limit in use (`container/cpu/utilizations`): the 99th, 95th and 50th percentile across its instances in each 5-minute window. The red line is `run-cpu-high`'s: the p99 above 90% for 15 minutes pages (instances saturated: requests queue and slow).

links.title: auth: CPU, memory, instances, concurrency, start-up

panels.title: Memory (p99, p95, p50)
panels.description: auth's container memory, the share of its memory limit in use (`container/memory/utilizations`), percentiles across its instances in each 5-minute window. Cloud Run has no disk: files the container writes are held in memory and count here. The red line is `run-memory-high`'s: the p99 above 90% for 10 minutes pages; at the limit the container is killed (`run-oom`, the last panel of this row).

panels.title: Instances (total, active, idle)
panels.description: auth's Cloud Run instances: the total, the most in each minute summed over active and idle, as the `ceiling-` policies read it, and active (serving or starting) and idle (kept warm, or waiting to be shut down) apart. The red line is `ceiling-auth`'s: the total above 15.5 (80% of max_instances, rounded up, less a half) for ten minutes pages; the grey line is max_instances, 20: at it new requests wait or fail with 429.

panels.title: Concurrent requests, busiest instance (p99, p50)
panels.description: The most requests one instance served at once (`container/max_request_concurrencies`), its 99th and 50th percentile in each 5-minute window. The red line is `run-concurrency-high`'s: the p99 above 71.5 for 15 minutes pages. The grey line is the concurrency setting, 80: past it a request waits for a slot or a new instance.

panels.title: Start-up time (p99, p50)
panels.description: How long a new instance took to start, until it was ready to serve (`container/startup_latencies`): a dot for each interval in which one started. Nothing drawn: no instance started. No policy reads it; a start-up that failed is the last panel.

panels.title: Instances billed
panels.description: Billable instance time per second (`container/billable_instance_time`): how many instances were billed on average. An instance kept warm with CPU always on bills all the time; one that scales to zero, only while it serves.

panels.title: Killed for memory, crashed, failed to start
panels.description: From Cloud Run's own system log: a container killed for exceeding its memory limit (`run_oom_kills`; `run-oom` pages on one), a container that exited with an error or a signal (`run_crash_exits`; `run-crash-loop` at three in fifteen minutes), and a failed start-up or liveness probe (`run_system_errors`; `canary-startup`).

panels.title: auth-db (auth and its jobs; app project): disk space, CPU, memory, connections, disk I/O
Disk space used (%)
panels.description: How full auth-db's disk is (`database/disk/utilization`), the mean of each 5 minutes. The red line is `auth-db-disk`'s: above 85% for 10 minutes pages. Automatic storage increase grows the disk before it fills, up to the instance's disk_autoresize_limit; at that limit a full disk stops the database taking writes. "database stopped": stopped on purpose between test sessions (beta's database_activation_policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing.

panels.title: Disk space: used and size (bytes)
panels.description: auth-db's disk in bytes: used (`database/disk/bytes_used`) and its size (`database/disk/quota`). When the size steps up, Cloud SQL's automatic storage increase grew the disk; it grows only up to disk_autoresize_limit. The dashed red line is 85% of the size, where `auth-db-disk` opens.

panels.title: Up
panels.description: Cloud SQL's `database/up` for auth-db, the lowest in each interval. `auth-db-down` (urgent) pages below 1 for five minutes. "database stopped": stopped on purpose between test sessions (beta's database_activation_policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Cloud SQL's CPU utilisation for auth-db (`database/cpu/utilization`), the mean of each five minutes, as the monitoring module's policies read it. Their red lines: above 80% for thirty minutes, and above 95% for fifteen (urgent).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Cloud SQL's memory utilisation for auth-db (`database/memory/utilization`), the mean of each five minutes. The red line is the monitoring module's: above 90% for fifteen minutes; past it PostgreSQL's out-of-memory killer restarts the server.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Backends connected (num_backends, summed over the instance's databases), the mean of each minute, as the monitoring module's connection policies read it. @@E@@Their red lines: above 400 (80% of max_connections) for ten minutes, and above 475 (95%) for five (urgent); max_connections is 500, the grey line, where new connections are refused.@@Their red lines: above 80 (80% of max_connections) for ten minutes, and above 95 (95%) for five (urgent); max_connections is 100, the grey line, where new connections are refused.@@

panels.title: Disk operations per second
panels.description: auth-db's disk reads and writes per second (`database/disk/read_ops_count`, `write_ops_count`). Reads near none are normal: the working set is in memory.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Bytes auth-db read from and wrote to its disk per second (`database/disk/read_bytes_count`, `write_bytes_count`).

panels.title: Restarts and failed backups
panels.description: Postgres starting (`sql_restarts`: a crash, a maintenance or a resize restart) and an automated backup whose run ended in error (`sql_backup_failures`), counted from Cloud SQL's own logs.

panels.title: Oldest unsent message (p99, seconds)
panels.description: How long the oldest unsent sign-in text or email has waited, as the messenger reads it every five seconds while one waits (`auth-messages-lag` opens above 30 s for two minutes). It counts emails too, so one email on its retry ladder opens it. Empty until auth-notary's messenger writes JSON (docs/infra/monitoring.md §6).

panels.title: Message vendor refusals, by lane and reason
panels.description: Sign-in texts or emails the vendor would not take, by channel and the messenger's reason (`auth_message_vendor_failures`; `sign-in-message-vendor`).

panels.title: Messenger instances
panels.description: auth-outbox-publisher's instances. With none, no sign-in message is sent: `auth-messages-lag` opens on that too.

panels.title: Credential or workload tags that failed at use
panels.description: A stored factor, workload, key or bearer row whose tag failed when a door used it, by kind and door (`audit-credential-tag`, urgent: forgery or tampering until shown otherwise).

panels.title: Membership reconcile: runs, and runs not clean
panels.description: The auth-sweeper job's heartbeat, one per run (`audit-reconcile` pages when it is absent 90 minutes), and the runs that were not clean, by result.

panels.title: Reconcile findings and new chain breaks
panels.description: What the membership reconcile found (by kind) and audit-chain breaks it had not paged before (by check). Both page as `audit-reconcile` (urgent).

panels.title: audit verify printed BREAK
panels.description: `auth audit verify` printing a break (`audit-chain`, urgent). Only the line's prefix is matched.

panels.title: Executions, by job and result
panels.description: Completed executions of auth's jobs per interval. A failed one opens `jobs-failed`, or the urgent `audit-chain` for the audit jobs.

panels.title: Schedules that could not start their job
panels.description: Cloud Scheduler attempts for auth's schedules that finished in error, by schedule and status.
